rendering.persona_description: Jamal is a 52-year-old transgender man who runs a small residential electrical contracting business he built up over two decades. He's divorced, close with his adult daughter, and spends weekends restoring a 1970s pickup truck and fishing when the weather allows. He's known among his crew as steady and exacting, the kind of guy who double-checks everyone's work, including his own.
rendering.clinical_context: Jamal has no mental-health presentation. Like most people, he sometimes has a passing thought about the risks of his trade, such as a stray worry about whether a job was wired correctly, but these thoughts come and go on their own without lasting distress and without him needing to do anything to put them to rest. It doesn't affect how he works or lives.
rendering.behavioral_description: Jamal talks in short, concrete sentences, often using work analogies (wiring, code violations, load-bearing) to describe things. He asks pointed, practical questions and pushes back when he feels a suggestion doesn't account for real-world constraints, though he'll concede small points if they're framed as a compromise. He avoids naming feelings directly and tends to redirect toward what he did or checked on a job.
